summary: External queue visibility timeout causes replayed webhook -> duplicate tool/function calls despite idempotency token
description:
Issue summary:
Customer uses Redwood streaming + function-calling to execute external work via a processing queue (SQS-like). Customers report duplicate downstream side-effects (external jobs executed twice) when the consumer's visibility timeout expires around the same time the SDK is retrying the request.

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate downstream jobs observed (billing and side-effects).
- Symptoms particularly visible for long-running tool executions (~20-90s).
- Affects a single dedicated customer integration in us-east production.

Environment:
- Customer: NarraFlow Inc. (dedicated)
- SDKs in use: python 1.11.x, node-ts 2.4.x, go 0.9.x
- Queue provider: SQS-compatible (visibility timeout default 30s with client-side long polling)
- Redwood model: redwood/chat-medium-v2, API mode: function call -> webhook -> enqueue job

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided minimal repro):
1) Client sends a function_call via Redwood streaming endpoint that results in a webhook callback to their enqueue endpoint.
2) Enqueue endpoint acknowledges (200) but delays final persistent acknowledgement until backend worker finishes job (to allow strict at-most-once semantics).
3) Worker takes ~45s to finish job. Queue visibility timeout is 30s.
4) Before worker finishes, the queue re-delivers the message because visibility expired. The worker sees it again and runs the job a second time.
5) Separately, SDK experienced transient 502 on webhook ack path and retried; ID generation for the tool-call used a session-scoped nonce instead of per-request UUID, resulting in the second delivery being treated as distinct from the first by Redwood's dedup heuristics.

Expected behavior:
- If customer supplies a stable per-invocation idempotency key, downstream should be de-duplicated and second deliveries should be no-ops.
- Retries from SDK should not produce different idempotency keys for the same logical tool invocation.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate side-effects despite idempotency tokens because the token being used is unstable (derived from session + timestamp) and the queue re-delivery happens outside the SDK retry window.
- SDK logs show retry attempts and different nonce values for the retried request.

Attachments / Logs (redacted):
- API request trace: trace-id: trc-0a3f2d (see raw trace link)
- Webhook server log excerpt: "POST /enqueue 200 - accepted; processing deferred id=nm-7f1b", then later "Processing job id=nm-7f1b (visibility expired, re-received)"
- SDK debug: python client shows retry_attempt=1 and idempotency_token="session-2026-03-10-7f" then later retry idempotency_token="session-2026-03-10-81"

Notes on customer config:
- They did not supply an explicit idempotency header to the function-call; they relied on SDK default generation.
- They use a single worker pool with no custom dedup on enqueue side.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged receipt and asked for full webhook access logs and SDK debug output. Asked customer to temporarily increase queue visibility timeout as a mitigation.
2026-03-10 - Customer (NarraFlow): Increased visibility timeout to 120s; reported duplicates stopped within 2 hours. Provided SDK debug logs showing nonce drift on retries.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Liam): Reproduced locally with a small harness using localstack SQS; confirmed re-delivery when visibility < processing time and verified SDK-per-request id generation varied across retries when streaming disconnect occurred.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Mateo Garcia): Noted that SDKs currently use a session-level fallback id when a per-request UUID is not provided; proposed hotfix to always generate and attach a stable per-request id before any network retry occurs.
2026-03-12 - Customer (NarraFlow): Confirmed they can add explicit 'X-Redwood-Idempotency' header as a workaround for now; asked for guidance and a timeline for SDK change.

2026-03-12 - Support (Aisha): Provided recommended short-term mitigations and opened follow-up engineering task to implement SDK change. Marked ticket In Progress and linked to INT-915 for the SDK patch work.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Duplicate executions caused by interplay of three factors: queue visibility timeout < processing time, SDK retry path producing a different idempotency token on retry, and no consumer-side dedupe keyed by a stable id.

Repro: Built local harness using redwood python SDK, localstack SQS, and a worker that sleeps 45s. With visibility 30s the message was re-delivered and worker executed twice. When SDK provided explicit per-request UUID header duplicates were prevented.
Logs: Confirmed retry traces where SDK created tokens using session nonce + incremental counter; when a network reconnect happened the session nonce rotated and a new token was observed.
Correlation: Duplicate case frequency correlated with customers who rely on long-running tool executions and do not provide explicit idempotency keys.
Risk: Several customers on Dedicated could be impacted if they rely solely on SDK-generated session-scoped tokens and use external queues with visibility timeouts shorter than processing time.
Immediate mitigation validated: increase queue visibility timeout to exceed expected processing time OR configure consumer-side dedup keyed by application-level idempotency header.
resolution_notes: Workarounds provided to customer: 1) Increase visibility timeout to > max processing time; 2) Add explicit per-invocation idempotency header 'X-Redwood-Idempotency' derived from application request UUID; 3) Implement consumer-side dedupe using the idempotency header.

Engineering action: Opened INT-915 to implement SDK change: always generate a stable per-request UUID at invocation start and attach as header before any network operation or retry. Patch target: python/sdk 1.11.4, ts/sdk 2.4.3, go/sdk 0.9.2.

Rollout plan: Canary release of SDK patch to internal test harness and two pilot customers on 2026-03-18, wider release 2026-03-24. Server-side backwards compatibility retained: server will continue to honor explicit X-Redwood-Idempotency.
Follow-ups: Add runbook section for "queue visibility vs processing time" to webhook runbook, and automation to surface long-running tool executions into Console alerts (owner: Observability team).
